commuterPass.elasticity.unit: percent change in ridership per percent change in fare

source.citation: Simpson-Curtin rule (fare elasticity of transit ridership of about -0.3), as reported in Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities (Victoria Transport Policy Institute)
source.url: https://www.vtpi.org/tranelas.pdf

estimated.method: Range ends cited via review; the original tables were not read. The individual Litman table entries for -0.5 and -0.2 are still to be read.

lowSource.citation: Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities: long-run values are larger in absolute size (the individual table entry for -0.5 is still to be read)

highSource.citation: Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities (the individual table entry for -0.2 is still to be read)

commuterPass.lag.assumption: The fare elasticities are short-run responses to a price change and are taken to act in the quarter of the change.

source.citation: Project assumption; fare elasticities in RESEARCH-NOTES 2e are short-run responses
source.url: .kiro/specs/data-pipeline/design.md

estimated.method: Assumed 0 quarters from the short-run elasticities. Data that would replace it: a measured time profile of ridership after a fare change in Taipei.

commuterPass.unitCost.unit: TWD of budget per TWD of subsidy
commuterPass.unitCost.assumption: One TWD of budget pays one TWD of subsidy, with no administration overhead.

source.citation: Project assumption; no administration overhead was found
source.url: .kiro/specs/data-pipeline/design.md

estimated.method: Assumed 1. Data that would replace it: published administration cost of the commuter pass and rent subsidy programs.

ghost.commuteThreshold.assumption: project rule; no study found for 60 minutes

source.citation: Project rule, no study for the value of 60 minutes. The 45-minute low end is a TVBS report on a survey of tolerable one-way commute time (original study unknown)
source.url: https://news.tvbs.com.tw/life/832402

lowSource.citation: TVBS report on a survey of tolerable one-way commute time (about 45 minutes); original study unknown

estimated.method: The low end is the survey figure as reported by TVBS. The value and the high end of 60 minutes are a project rule, without a cited study. A MOTC daily transport survey, reported by TVBS in 2017, gives about 57 minutes for trips from New Taipei City to Taipei City.

source.citation: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), definition of a severely cost-burdened household (rent above 50 percent of income)
source.url: https://www.huduser.gov/portal/node/10587

ghost.sensitivityCommute.unit: share of employed residents per minute of one-way commute time

source.citation: DGBAS, 2020 Population and Housing Census, table 14 (employed residents by place of work), Taipei City and New Taipei City reports; Open Government Data License 1.0
source.url: https://data.gov.tw/dataset/10906

estimated.method: ghost.sensitivityCommute = share of the same estimated workplace distribution whose time lies above 59 and at most 60 minutes; it is the change of the share above 60 minutes per 1 minute of commute time. The workplace distribution is estimated as for ghost.shareCommuteWithin: same-district commutes count as 0 minutes, other districts of the same city and the other city of the pair are weighted by commute.jobShare. The placement of the category of workers in another county, city or overseas into the other city of the pair can shift mass across the threshold, so the Ghost counts derived from it may be under-estimated.

ghost.sensitivityRent.unit: share of renter persons per percentage point of rent burden

source.citation: Ministry of Finance (Fiscal Information Agency), comprehensive income tax statistics by village, income year 2023 (112_165-9.csv); Open Government Data License 1.0
source.url: https://data.gov.tw/dataset/103066

estimated.method: ghost.sensitivityRent = sum over the 41 districts of renter persons x (P(burden > 49) - P(burden > 50)), divided by total renter persons; this is the change of the share per 1 percentage point of burden. Renter persons are 2023Q4 population x renterRate(city). Reference year 2023, the last year with observed FIA data (2024 and 2025 are extrapolated). Household income of each district is assumed log-normal. Its median is the mean of the district householdIncome indicator over the four quarters of 2023, which is the income the engine uses. Its scale is (ln Q3 - ln Q1) / (2 x 0.6745) from the first and third quartile of the district total row of the FIA file for income year 2023, so the spread is that of FIA income: FIA income is per tax unit, not per household, and excludes transfer income (for example pensions, allowances and subsidies), so it can be more or less dispersed than household disposable income. The log-normal form is a two-parameter approximation: it has no heavy upper tail or mass at low incomes, and the tail at a burden near the threshold depends on that form. Renters are assumed to have the same income distribution as all households of the district, although renter households usually have lower income, which would raise the share. The rent of the reference dwelling is the district mean 2023 rent indicator multiplied by housing.dwellingSize. Burden is monthly rent divided by monthly income (annual income / 12), in percent; a household has a rent burden above the threshold when its income is below 1200 x rent / threshold. The renter rate is the 2020 census value of the city (a single-year value) applied to the 2023Q4 population of each district.

estimated.method: ghost.shareCommuteWithin = share of the employed residents of the 41 districts (2020 census table 14) whose one-way time in the Commute_Matrix to the workplace district is at most 60 minutes; the range low is the share at most 45 minutes and the range high equals the value. Table 14 gives, for each residence district, the employed residents working in the same district, in another district of the same city, and in another county, city or overseas, and it gives no count by workplace district. Workplace districts are therefore estimated: residents working in the same district have time 0; residents working in another district of the same city are spread over the other districts of that city in proportion to commute.jobShare; residents working in another county, city or overseas are spread over the districts of the other city of the pair in proportion to commute.jobShare. Effect of the spreading, in both directions. (a) Setting commutes within one district to 0 minutes barely changes the share within the threshold, because commutes inside one district are under 45 minutes. (b) Placing the whole category of workers in another county, city or overseas into the other city of the pair raises the share within the threshold when the real destinations lie outside both cities (for example Linkou or Shulin to Taoyuan, and Xizhi to Keelung, are longer trips), so the Ghost counts derived from this share may be under-estimated. Commute times come from the modelled Commute_Matrix, and the census counts are for 2020 only.

highSource.citation: TDX Rail/Metro ODFare, Taipei Metro (TRTC), New Taipei Metro (NTMC), Danhai LRT (NTDLRT) and Ankeng LRT (NTALRT), adult single-journey full fare, Ministry of Transport and Communications

estimated.method: Regression: least squares with an intercept of the adult full fare (TWD) on the rail-graph in-vehicle path time (minutes) over 14774 station pairs gives 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip; value is this slope multiplied by the monthly trips. Selection: high is the larger of value and the same regression over the Uncapped_Range multiplied by the monthly trips, 0.6928 TWD per minute per trip. The Uncapped_Range is the 14603 pairs with a path time below 59.783333333333324 minutes, the shortest pair charged the Fare_Cap of 65 TWD. low is 0, the marginal cost of a minute for a pass holder. Monthly trips: commute.tripsPerMonth = 44 one-way trips per commuter per month, Parameter_Status gap. Fare cap: fares are capped (maximum 65 TWD), so a linear per-minute cost over-estimates long trips. The Fare_Cap affects only 48 of 14,774 station pairs (0.3 percent). The slope does not rise after excluding them (0.6928 against 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip), so high equals value (30.60). The uncertainty range is provided by low = 0. Stations not in the network: R01, V01, V02, V03, V04, V05, V06, V07, V08, V09, V10, V11, V26, V27, V28 do not appear in the TDX station-to-station travel time files or the Ankeng StationTimeTable run times; 424 station pairs are excluded. Migration weights: the fares are cited, but the migration weights (migration.weight*, migration.threshold, migration.share) are gap, so how strongly the commuter pass subsidy moves migration is an assumption. Backtest: the TPASS backtest validates MRT entries only and does not validate migration.

estimated.method: migration.exitShare = (total registered move-outs - moves to the other city - moves to another district of the same city) / total registered move-outs, summed over all villages and the 120 months of 2016Q1 to 2025Q4 (3253971 move-outs, 2018955 of them within the two cities). Destinations outside the two cities include abroad, Taoyuan, other counties and cities, and cancelled registrations.

migration.exitShare.assumption: The share of residents who leave their district under rent pressure and also leave the two cities is assumed equal to the share of all registered move-outs that go outside the two cities. This is only an approximation: the files give the destination at the level of city or county and not district to district, they hold all moves and not only moves driven by rent burden, and the registered total includes cancelled registrations and "other" cases whose destination is unknown, which count as exits. Residents who leave because of rent may go to Taoyuan or Keelung more often or less often than other movers. A published measure of the destinations of rent-driven movers would replace it. This value is an assumption and not a research result.

estimated.method: migration.share = mean of moveOut / population over 1640 district-quarters (41 districts, 2016Q1 to 2025Q4); moveOut is the registered move-out count of the quarter (all destinations, including moves between districts of the same city) and population is the end-of-quarter population.

migration.share.assumption: The share of residents who leave when the burden excess passes the threshold is assumed equal to the ordinary quarterly move-out rate. This is only an approximation: the registered rate measures all moves, made for any reason (work, family, housing), not moves caused by a rise in rent burden, and the baseline already contains this ordinary movement, so the simulated movement partly counts it again. No study of the share of residents who leave because of a rent-burden rise in Taipei or New Taipei was found. A published measure of rent-driven displacement for the two cities, for example from a household survey of reasons for moving, would replace it. This value is an assumption and not a research result.

source.citation: Computed from the baseline rent indicator (Ministry of the Interior actual-price registration rental records), the householdIncome indicator (DGBAS Survey of Family Income and Expenditure with the 2021 Industry, Commerce and Services Census), and housing.dwellingSize; Open Government Data License 1.0
source.url: https://plvr.land.moi.gov.tw/DownloadOpenData

estimated.method: migration.threshold = population standard deviation, over 1640 district-quarters (41 districts, 2016Q1 to 2025Q4), of the 4-quarter change of baseline rent burden in percentage points, rounded to 0.1. Burden = rent * housing.dwellingSize (89.9 m2) / (householdIncome / 12) * 100. Each quarter is compared with the same quarter one year earlier, so consecutive changes overlap.

migration.threshold.assumption: A rent-burden rise is assumed to move people only when it exceeds the ordinary year-to-year variation of the burden across districts. This is only an approximation: the spread of the baseline measures how much burden varied in the past for any reason, including income estimates that are interpolated, and not the rise at which households decide to move. No study of the rent-burden rise that triggers a move in Taipei or New Taipei was found. A household survey or panel study of rent burden before and after moves in the two cities would replace it. This value is an assumption and not a research result.
